svg.title: GHK-Cu: from failed wound drug to skin cream to injectable
svg.desc: 1973: Loren Pickart's PhD work: a factor in human blood helps liver cells survive; 1977: The factor is identified as the tripeptide glycyl-histidyl-lysine (GHK); 1980: Nature paper: GHK binds copper and carries it into cells; 1985: Pickart starts ProCyte to make GHK-Cu (Iamin) a wound-healing drug; 1992: Venous ulcer trial: copper tripeptide cream no better than placebo; 1994: 511-patient Phase III fails; stock falls 68% in a day; 35% of staff cut; 1996: FDA clears Iamin gel as a wound dressing (device route: safety, not proof it heals); 1997: Japanese partner quits: it's a device in the US, not a drug; 1998: ProCyte sells copper peptides into prestige skin care (Saks, Neiman Marcus); 2014: Pickart's Skin Biology: GHK changes 31% of genes, in 2 cancer cell lines; 2026: FDA committee review of GHK-Cu due by Feb 2027; injectable-risk warning stays

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
